texts.li: The first warm days are here, and winter's dirt is in every corner: tracked mud, ash, things put down and never picked up. {A_nameDef} wants a day of it, everyone with a broom, and a toast in a clean room after.
{A_nameDef} opened every door this morning to let the spring in, and didn't like what it showed. {A_nameDef} asks for a day for the cleaning, all hands, before the sowing takes everyone.
[again] The warm days are back, and so is the dirt. {A_nameDef} has the brooms out already, and asks whether it's to be a day of spring cleaning again.
[tradition] It's the time of year for the spring cleaning, and {A_nameDef} has been counting buckets. The colony has kept the day for years now.
[missed] Last spring the cleaning was let go, and the colony felt it all year. {A_nameDef} asks that it not happen twice.

li.label: All hands for a day
li.outcome: They cleaned from one end of the colony to the other, then carried everything lying about to where it belongs, and finished with a toast in a room that smelled of soap.

outcomes.li: [years] The spring cleaning went the way it always does: brooms first, then the hauling, then a toast. Someone found a thing that went missing last autumn.

lines.li: Behind the shelves too, it's spring.
Whose boots are these, and why are they here?
Sweep it out the door, not under the rug.
I found the good knife under here.

li.label: a toast in a clean room
The morning only
li.outcome: Four of them cleaned and hauled through the morning, and the rest got on with the day. The worst of it is gone.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The dirt can wait for the cleaners' own time, and the day's work goes on. {A_nameDef} put the brooms back, slowly.

texts.li: A warm, dry day, and {A_nameDef} wants the colony to walk its bounds: all round the edge of the land, stopping at every turn to set a stone, so the young ones grow up knowing where home ends.
{A_nameDef} grew up walking the bounds every summer, and says a place isn't really yours until you've walked all the way round it together. It would take the morning.
[again] The bounds want walking again, {A_nameDef} says, and the stones want finding.
[tradition] It's bounds-walking weather. {A_nameDef} has a list of every stone they set, and wants to see them all again.
[missed] Nobody walked the bounds last summer, and {A_nameDef} wonders aloud whether the stones are still where they were left.

li.label: Everyone walks the bounds
li.outcome: The colony walked all round its edge in the morning sun, stopping at every turn, and set a stone at each one. The children ran ahead to find the next.

outcomes.li: [again] They walked the bounds again and found the stones where they'd left them, and set new ones where any had gone. The children knew the way this time.

lines.li: This is where our land ends, remember it.
Set it straight, it has to last.
Is that the stone from last year?
One more turn and we're halfway round.

li.label: {A_nameDef} walks it with one other
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and one other walked the bounds and set the stones. It was quicker, and the young ones stayed home.

li.label: Not this year
li.outcome: The bounds can stay unwalked another year, and the morning's work goes on. {A_nameDef} didn't say much at supper.

texts.li: It's a clear, warm evening without a cloud, and {A_nameDef} wants everyone outside tonight: blankets on the ground, lights out, and the whole sky. It would mean a late night, and a late start tomorrow.
{A_nameDef} has been watching the sky all week and says tonight will be the clearest yet. {A_nameDef} wants to sit out late with everyone and name what's up there.
[again] Another clear summer night, and {A_nameDef} already has the blankets out for the star night.
[tradition] It's the star night, and {A_nameDef} has been waiting for a sky like this one all summer.

li.label: Everyone sits out late
li.outcome: They lay out on blankets until long past midnight while {A_nameDef} named the stars, some of them correctly. Everyone slept late the next morning.

outcomes.li: [years] The star night, as every summer: blankets, the same stars named the same wrong way, and a slow morning after.

lines.li: That one isn't a star, it moves.
Lie down, you see more lying down.
Which one's ours, do you think?

li.label: An hour under the stars, then bed
li.outcome: They sat out for an hour and looked up, and went to bed at the usual time with stiff necks.

li.label: Bed as usual
li.outcome: Everyone went to bed at the usual time, and was up for work at the usual time. {A_nameDef} sat by the window a while first.

texts.li: The water is warm and the fish are rising, and {A_nameDef} wants a fishing match: everyone who can hold a line out at the water for the afternoon, and whatever they catch cooked for supper after.
{A_nameDef} swears {A_pronoun} can out-fish anyone in the colony, and {B_nameDef} has laughed at that once too often. {A_nameDef} wants to settle it with a match, and a fish supper for everyone.
[again] It's fishing weather, and {A_nameDef} wants the match again, if only to win it this time.
[tradition] The fishing match comes round with the summer, and {A_nameDef} has been sharpening hooks for a week.

li.label: A match and a fish supper
li.outcome: The colony fished all afternoon and argued about the biggest catch all through supper. Nobody agrees who won.

lines.li: That one counts, it was this big.
Mine's bigger and you know it.

li.label: A quiet afternoon for two
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon at the water with a line each, and came back with fish and a story each about the one that got away.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: No match this summer, and nobody leaves their work for the water. {A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} would have won.

texts.li: The meat in the stores won't see the colony through the winter, and there's game on the land. {A_nameDef} wants a proper autumn hunt: three hunters out after several beasts, and fresh meat for supper.
{A_nameDef} has been watching the herds move across the far side of the land all week. Before the cold comes, {A_pronoun} says, the colony should hunt, and eat well the night it does.
[again] It's the season for the autumn hunt again, and {A_nameDef} has been oiling the bows.
[tradition] The autumn hunt is a custom here now, and {A_nameDef} has picked the game already.

li.label: A big hunt, and supper after
li.outcome: The hunters went out together and came back with the game slung between them. The whole colony ate at one table that night.

li.label: One hunter, one beast
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went out alone after one good beast, and the stores are a little fuller for it.

li.label: No hunt this year
li.outcome: No autumn hunt. The stores will have to do, or the traders. {A_nameDef} hung the bow back on its peg.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}, who keeps the colony's bees, says there's news the bees should hear, and that it's done hive by hive, by the family, the old way.
[news:death] Someone of the colony has died, and {A_nameDef} says the bees must be told, hive by hive, or they'll grieve without knowing why.
[news:birth] There's a new child in the colony, and {A_nameDef} wants to go round the hives and tell the bees before anyone else outside the family hears.
[news:wedding] Two of the colony are married, and {A_nameDef} says the bees must hear it from the family, hive by hive.
[tradition] There's news, and the colony tells the bees its news: {A_nameDef} is waiting at the first hive.

li.label: The family walks round the hives with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: They went from hive to hive with {A_nameDef}, and at each one {A_nameDef} knocked and told the bees the news in a low voice.

outcomes.li: [news:death] They went from hive to hive, and at each one {A_nameDef} told the bees who was gone. Someone tied a strip of black cloth to every hive.
[news:birth] At each hive {A_nameDef} told the bees the new child's name, and the bees went on humming.

lines.li: Bees, there is news, so listen.
Knock gently, they don't like a fuss.

li.label: {A_nameDef} goes round alone
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went from hive to hive alone and told the bees the news at each one.

li.label: It isn't done here
li.outcome: Nobody went to the hives. The bees went on with their work. {A_nameDef} looked at them a long while all the same.
